# AngularVelocity

- Inherits [`Constraint`](constraint.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("AngularVelocity")`

Keeps the part that `Attachment0` is on spinning at a set rate, using up to `MaxTorque`. Use it for a fan, a turning coin or a planet. It is solved together with the joints the part is in, so a hinged door turns about its hinge. For a wheel on an axle, a `HingeConstraint` with a motor is usually the better choice.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AngularVelocity` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | The spin to hold, in radians per second about each axis of the frame that `RelativeTo` names. |
| `MaxTorque` | `number` | `10000` | read/write | The largest torque the constraint can apply, in newton meters, about each axis of the part. |
| `ReactionTorqueEnabled` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether an equal and opposite torque is applied to the part that `Attachment1` is on, like a motor twisting its mount. With it on, the spin is measured between the two parts. |
| `RelativeTo` | `Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo` | `Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World` | read/write | The frame the spin is given in: the world, or an attachment. |
